questions.q: Which part of the CPU carries out arithmetic and logical operations?
questions.explanation: The ALU performs additions, subtractions, comparisons and logical operations, while the control unit directs the flow of instructions.

questions.q: Which of these is volatile memory, losing its contents when the power is switched off?
questions.explanation: RAM is volatile main memory; ROM, hard disks and flash drives keep their data without power.

questions.q: Which of the following is system software?
questions.explanation: An operating system manages hardware and provides a platform for other programs, so it is system software.

questions.q: A translator that reads the whole source program and converts it into machine code before the program runs is called a
questions.explanation: A compiler translates the entire program at once and reports errors after scanning it; an interpreter works statement by statement.

questions.q: A translator that translates and executes a program one statement at a time is called a/an
questions.explanation: An interpreter translates and runs each statement in turn, stopping at the first error it meets.

questions.q: Which list arranges memory from fastest to slowest?
questions.explanation: Registers sit inside the CPU and are fastest, then cache, then main memory (RAM), then secondary storage such as a hard disk.

questions.q: Why is a small, fast cache memory placed between the CPU and the RAM?
options: The CPU is much faster than RAM, so keeping frequently used data in cache reduces waiting time
RAM cannot store instructions, only cache can
Cache memory is non-volatile and keeps programs permanently
Cache increases the storage capacity of the hard disk
questions.explanation: The CPU can execute instructions faster than RAM can supply data, so cache holds recently used data close to the CPU and cuts the delay.

questions.q: Differentiate between system software and application software, giving one example of each.
questions.answer: System software manages and controls the hardware and provides a platform for other programs (e.g. an operating system). Application software helps users perform a specific task (e.g. a word processor).
keyPoints: System software controls hardware and the computer's resources
questions.explanation: System software supports the computer itself, while application software serves the user's particular needs.

questions.q: What is the base of the hexadecimal number system?
questions.explanation: Hexadecimal uses 16 symbols: 0 to 9 and A to F.

questions.q: What is the binary equivalent of the decimal number 13?
questions.explanation: 13 = 8 + 4 + 1, which is 1101 in binary.

questions.q: What is the decimal value of the binary number 10110?
What is the decimal value of the hexadecimal number 2F?
What is the octal equivalent of the binary number 101110?
questions.explanation: Group the bits in threes: 101 = 5 and 110 = 6, so the octal number is 56.

questions.q: What is the sum of the binary numbers 1010 and 0111?
questions.explanation: 1010 is 10 and 0111 is 7; 10 + 7 = 17, which is 10001 in binary.

questions.q: What is the minimum number of bits needed to store any whole number from 0 to 100?
questions.explanation: 6 bits store up to 63 and 7 bits store up to 127, so 7 bits are the minimum.

questions.q: Convert the decimal number 45 into binary, showing the method.
questions.answer: Divide repeatedly by 2: 45 -> remainder 1, 22 -> 0, 11 -> 1, 5 -> 1, 2 -> 0, 1 -> 1. Reading the remainders from bottom to top gives 101101.
keyPoints: Remainders read from last to first
questions.explanation: 32 + 8 + 4 + 1 = 45, which confirms 101101.

questions.q: Convert the hexadecimal number 3A into binary and into decimal.
questions.answer: 3 = 0011 and A = 1010, so 3A is 00111010, i.e. 111010 in binary. In decimal it is 3 x 16 + 10 = 58.
questions.explanation: Binary 111010 = 32 + 16 + 8 + 2 = 58, matching the direct hex conversion.

questions.q: When is the output of a two-input AND gate equal to 1?
options: When at least one input is 1
questions.explanation: AND outputs 1 only if every input is 1.

questions.q: Which gate outputs 1 only when its two inputs are different?
questions.explanation: XOR (exclusive OR) is 1 when exactly one of its inputs is 1.

questions.q: According to De Morgan's law, NOT (A AND B) is equal to
questions.explanation: De Morgan's law: the complement of a product is the sum of the complements, (A.B)' = A' + B'.

questions.q: For how many of the four possible input combinations of A and B is A XOR B equal to 1?
questions.explanation: XOR is 1 for (0,1) and (1,0) only, so for two combinations.

questions.q: Which pair of gates is called universal, because any logic circuit can be built from either one alone?
questions.explanation: Every other gate can be built using only NAND gates, or only NOR gates.

questions.q: By the absorption law, A + A.B simplifies to
How many rows does the truth table of a Boolean expression with three input variables have?
questions.explanation: Each variable can be 0 or 1, so there are 2 x 2 x 2 = 8 combinations.

questions.q: State De Morgan's two laws using Boolean notation.
questions.answer: (A.B)' = A' + B' and (A + B)' = A'.B'. The complement of an AND is the OR of the complements, and the complement of an OR is the AND of the complements.
questions.explanation: These laws let AND be converted to OR (and back) by complementing the terms.

questions.q: Simplify the expression A.B + A.B' using Boolean laws.
questions.explanation: Taking A common and using the complement law gives A.

questions.q: A finite, ordered set of steps for solving a problem is called a/an
questions.explanation: An algorithm is a step-by-step procedure that solves a problem in a finite number of steps.

questions.q: Which flowchart symbol is used to show a decision (a yes/no or true/false test)?
questions.explanation: A diamond has two exits, for the outcomes of the condition; rectangles show processing and ovals show start/stop.

questions.q: Which of these is NOT a desirable property of a good algorithm?
options: It has steps that can be interpreted in more than one way
It finishes after a finite number of steps
Each step is clear and definite
questions.explanation: An algorithm must be unambiguous (definite); ambiguity makes it unusable.

questions.q: An algorithm repeatedly compares the target with the middle item of a sorted list and discards half of the list each time. This is
questions.explanation: Halving the search range using the middle element is the idea of binary search.

questions.q: In computational thinking, decomposition means
options: Breaking a complex problem into smaller, manageable parts
questions.explanation: Decomposition splits a big problem into smaller sub-problems that are easier to solve.

questions.q: A linear search is run on an unsorted list of 50 items for a value that is not in the list. How many comparisons are made?
questions.explanation: The value is absent, so every one of the 50 items must be compared with it.

questions.q: Why must a list be sorted before binary search can be applied?
options: Because the middle item cannot be found in an unsorted list
Because comparing with the middle item tells which half cannot contain the target only if the data is in order
Because sorted lists use less memory
Because binary search only works on numbers that are even
questions.explanation: Discarding half the list is justified only when the values are ordered; otherwise the target could be in either half.

questions.q: Write an algorithm in simple steps to find whether a given number is even or odd.
questions.answer: 1. Start. 2. Read the number N. 3. Divide N by 2 and find the remainder. 4. If the remainder is 0, print 'Even'; otherwise print 'Odd'. 5. Stop.
keyPoints: Check the remainder on division by 2
Print the result based on the condition
questions.explanation: A number is even exactly when N mod 2 equals 0.

questions.q: Which of the following is a valid Python variable name?
questions.explanation: Names cannot start with a digit, contain a hyphen, or be a keyword such as class; my_name is valid.

questions.q:
What is the output of the following code?
print(7 // 2, 7 % 2)
questions.explanation: // gives the floor quotient 3 and % gives the remainder 1.

questions.q:
What is the output of the following code?
print(2 ** 3 ** 2)
questions.explanation: ** is right-associative, so it is 2 ** (3 ** 2) = 2 ** 9 = 512.

questions.q:
What is the output of the following code?
x = 5
x += 3
x *= 2
print(x)
questions.explanation: x becomes 8 after += 3, and 16 after *= 2.

questions.q:
What is the output of the following code?
print('5' + '3', 5 + 3)
questions.explanation: + joins the strings '5' and '3' into '53', but adds the integers 5 and 3 to give 8.

questions.q:
What is the output of the following code?
print(-7 // 2, -7 % 3)
questions.explanation: // floors the quotient, so -7 // 2 = -4; % takes the sign of the divisor, so -7 % 3 = 2.

questions.q:
What is the output of the following code?
print(bool(0), bool('0'))
questions.explanation: The integer 0 is falsy, but the string '0' is a non-empty string and is truthy.

questions.q: What is the difference between the / and // operators in Python? Illustrate with 7 and 2.
questions.answer: / performs true division and always returns a float, so 7 / 2 gives 3.5. // performs floor division and discards the fractional part, so 7 // 2 gives 3.
keyPoints: // returns the floor of the quotient
questions.explanation: Floor division rounds down to the nearest whole number.

questions.q:
What does the following code print, and what does it show?
a, b = 3, 4
a, b = b, a
print(a, b)
questions.answer: It prints 4 3. The right-hand side (b, a) is evaluated first as (4, 3) and then assigned to a and b, so the values are swapped without a temporary variable.
keyPoints: Values are swapped without a temporary variable
questions.explanation: Tuple packing and unpacking makes the swap possible in one statement.
range(2, 10, 3) starts at 2 and steps by 3 while below 10: 2, 5, 8.

questions.q: Which statement skips the rest of the current loop iteration and moves on to the next one?
questions.explanation: continue jumps to the next iteration, whereas break ends the loop completely.

questions.q:
What is the output of the following code?
t = 0
for n in range(1, 5):
    t += n
print(t)
questions.explanation: range(1, 5) gives 1, 2, 3, 4, whose sum is 10.
The loop prints 0, 1, 2 and stops when i becomes 3, before printing it.
Even values of i are skipped, so only 1 and 3 are printed.
The inner loop runs 1, 2 and 3 times for i = 1, 2, 3, so c = 1 + 2 + 3 = 6.
The else block of a for loop runs when the loop ends without break; the last value of i is 2.

questions.q: Distinguish between the break and continue statements in a loop.
questions.answer: break terminates the loop immediately and control passes to the statement after the loop. continue skips the remaining statements of the current iteration and goes to the next iteration of the loop.
keyPoints: continue skips only the current iteration
questions.explanation: Both change the normal flow of a loop, but only break ends it.

questions.q: Write a Python program fragment that prints the table of 5 from 5 x 1 to 5 x 10 (only the products).
questions.answer:
for i in range(1, 11):
    print(5 * i)
questions.explanation: range stops before 11, so the loop runs ten times.

questions.q:
What is the output of the following code?
s = 'Computer'
print(s[1:4])
questions.explanation: Slicing from index 1 up to but not including index 4 gives 'omp'.

questions.q: What does len('Python') return?
questions.explanation: 'Python' has six characters.

questions.q:
What is the output of the following code?
s = 'Computer'
print(s[-3:])
questions.explanation: A negative start index counts from the end, so s[-3:] is the last three characters.

questions.q:
What is the output of the following code?
s = 'banana'
print(s.count('a'), s.find('n'))
questions.explanation: 'a' occurs three times, and the first 'n' is at index 2.

questions.q:
What is the output of the following code?
print('a,b,,c'.split(','))
questions.explanation: split(',') cuts at every comma, so the two adjacent commas leave an empty string between them.

questions.q:
What is the output of the following code?
print('abc' * 2 + 'd')
questions.explanation: 'abc' * 2 repeats the string to 'abcabc', and + 'd' appends d.

questions.q:
What is the output of the following code?
s = 'Computer'
print(s[::-1])
questions.explanation: A step of -1 reads the string backwards, giving 'retupmoC' with the capital C at the end.

questions.q:
What is the output of the following code?
print('-'.join(['a', 'b', 'c']), 'py'.isalpha(), '12a'.isdigit())
questions.explanation: join puts '-' between the items, 'py' is all letters, and '12a' contains a letter so isdigit() is False.

questions.q: Strings in Python are immutable. What happens when s = 'cat' is followed by s[0] = 'b', and how can you obtain 'bat'?
questions.answer: The assignment raises a TypeError because a string does not support item assignment. To get 'bat', build a new string: s = 'b' + s[1:].
keyPoints: Strings cannot be changed in place
Create a new string with slicing and concatenation
questions.explanation: Any change to a string actually produces a new string object.

questions.q: Which brackets are used to create a list in Python?
questions.explanation: Lists are written inside square brackets, for example [1, 2, 3].

questions.q: Which statement about tuples is correct?
options: Elements can be added with append()
Elements can be changed by assignment
A tuple cannot be changed after creation
A tuple can hold only numbers
questions.explanation: Tuples are immutable; their elements cannot be modified, added or removed.

questions.q:
What is the output of the following code?
L = [1, 2, 3]
L.append(4)
L.insert(1, 9)
print(L)
questions.explanation: append adds 4 at the end, then insert(1, 9) puts 9 at index 1.

questions.q:
What is the output of the following code?
L = [5, 2, 8, 1]
print(L[::2])
questions.explanation: A step of 2 takes the elements at indices 0 and 2, which are 5 and 8.

questions.q:
What is the output of the following code?
print(len((5,)), type((5)))
questions.explanation: (5,) is a one-element tuple, but (5) is just the integer 5 in brackets.

questions.q:
What is the output of the following code?
L = [1, 2, 3, 4]
print(L.pop(), L.pop(0), L)
questions.explanation: pop() removes the last item (4), pop(0) removes the first (1), leaving [2, 3].

questions.q:
What is the output of the following code?
L = [1, 2, 3]
M = L
M.append(4)
print(L)
questions.explanation: M = L makes both names refer to the same list, so appending through M also changes L.

questions.q:
What is the output of the following code?
L = [1, 2, 3]
M = L[:]
M.append(4)
print(L, M)
questions.explanation: L[:] creates a separate copy, so only M gets the new element.

questions.q: State two differences between a list and a tuple in Python.
questions.answer: A list is mutable (its elements can be changed, added or removed) and is written in square brackets, whereas a tuple is immutable and is written in parentheses. Tuples are generally used for fixed collections of data.
keyPoints: List is mutable, tuple is immutable
questions.explanation: Mutability is the key difference between the two sequence types.

questions.q: A Python dictionary stores its data as
questions.explanation: A dictionary maps unique keys to values.

questions.q: Which of the following can be used as a dictionary key?
questions.explanation: Keys must be immutable (hashable); a tuple of numbers qualifies, but lists, sets and dictionaries do not.

questions.q:
What is the output of the following code?
d = {'a': 1, 'b': 2}
d['c'] = 3
print(len(d), d.get('z', 0))
questions.explanation: Adding key 'c' makes three items, and get returns the default 0 for the missing key 'z'.

questions.q:
What is the output of the following code?
d = {'a': 1}
d['a'] = 5
d['a'] += 1
print(d)
questions.explanation: The key 'a' is given 5, then increased by 1, so its value is 6; keys are unique.
items() gives (key, value) pairs; each is printed followed by ';' with no newline.
pop removes the key and returns its value 1, leaving {'y': 2}.
The in operator checks keys only: 2 is a key, but 'a' is a value.

questions.q: Write code to count how many times each character occurs in the string 'hello', and give the output.
keyPoints: Use get(ch, 0) + 1 to update the count
questions.explanation: get supplies 0 for a character seen for the first time.

questions.q: Which keyword is used to define a function in Python?
questions.explanation: Functions are defined with the def keyword.

questions.q: Which standard module provides the sqrt() function?
questions.explanation: sqrt is in the math module, used as math.sqrt(x) after import math.

questions.q:
What is the output of the following code?
def f(x, y=2):
    return x * y
print(f(3), f(3, 4), f(y=5, x=1))
questions.explanation: f(3) uses the default y = 2; f(3, 4) = 12; keyword arguments give f(y=5, x=1) = 5.

questions.q:
What is the output of the following code?
def f(n):
    n += 1
print(f(1))
questions.explanation: The function has no return statement, so it returns None, which print displays.
*a collects any number of positional arguments into a tuple; with none it is empty (length 0).

questions.q:
What is the output of the following code?
import math
print(math.sqrt(16), math.floor(2.7), math.ceil(2.1))
questions.explanation: sqrt returns a float (4.0); floor(2.7) = 2 and ceil(2.1) = 3.

questions.q:
What is the output of the following code?
x = 10
def g():
    x = 5
    return x
print(g(), x)
questions.explanation: The x inside g is a local variable that does not change the global x, which stays 10.
f(5) = 5 x 4 x 3 x 2 x 1 = 120, since the function calls itself until n reaches 1.

questions.q: What is the difference between a parameter and an argument?
questions.answer: A parameter is the variable named in the function definition that receives a value. An argument is the actual value passed to the function when it is called. For example, in def f(x) the name x is a parameter, and in f(10) the value 10 is an argument.
keyPoints: Argument is the value supplied in the call
questions.explanation: Arguments are matched to parameters when the function runs.

questions.q: Gaining unauthorised access to a computer system or network is called
questions.explanation: Hacking is breaking into a system without permission, which is an offence under cyber law.

questions.q: Sending fake emails that appear genuine in order to steal a person's login details is called
questions.explanation: Phishing tricks users into revealing sensitive information through fake messages or websites.

questions.q: Which of these is the strongest password?
options: A mix of upper and lower case letters, digits and symbols, with no personal details
questions.explanation: Long, unpredictable passwords that mix character types are hard to guess, unlike common words or personal data.

questions.q: Using or copying software without the proper licence is known as
questions.explanation: Software piracy is the unauthorised copying, use or distribution of licensed software.

questions.q: What is the most responsible way to dispose of an old, broken mobile phone?
options: Hand it over to an authorised e-waste recycler
Throw it in the household dustbin
questions.explanation: E-waste contains harmful materials as well as recoverable metals, so authorised recycling is safest.

questions.q: A student posts public comments online. Years later, a college reads them while reviewing the application. This illustrates the idea of a
questions.explanation: A digital footprint is the trail of data a person leaves online, and it can persist for a long time.

questions.q: What is true of open-source software?
options: It can never be used for commercial purposes
Its source code is available, and users may study, modify and share it under the terms of its licence
It has no licence at all
It cannot be changed by anyone except the original author
questions.explanation: Open-source software publishes its source code and permits modification and redistribution, subject to its licence.

questions.q: What is phishing? Give two precautions to avoid it.
questions.answer: Phishing is a cyber fraud in which attackers send fake emails, messages or websites that look genuine to trick users into giving passwords, card or bank details. Precautions: do not click on suspicious links or attachments, check the sender's address and the website address, and never share OTPs or passwords.
keyPoints: Fake messages that appear genuine to steal information
questions.explanation: Careful checking of the sender and link before acting defeats most phishing attempts.

questions.q: Artificial Intelligence is best described as
options: A machine's ability to perform tasks that normally need human intelligence
questions.explanation: AI refers to systems that do tasks such as understanding language, recognising images or making decisions.

questions.q: Machine learning is a branch of AI in which
options: Computers are programmed with every possible answer
A system learns patterns from data instead of following only fixed rules
questions.explanation: In machine learning, algorithms improve their performance by finding patterns in data.

questions.q: Who proposed the well-known test in which a machine is judged by whether it can converse like a human?
questions.explanation: Alan Turing proposed this imitation test, now called the Turing test.

questions.q: Supervised learning is trained using
options: Data with no information at all
Labelled examples with known correct answers
questions.explanation: In supervised learning each training example comes with its correct label or output.

questions.q: Which of the following is a classification task?
options: Deciding whether an email is spam or not spam
Predicting a house's price as a number
Estimating the weight of a parcel
questions.explanation: Classification assigns an item to a category; predicting a numeric value is regression.

questions.q: Why is a separate test data set kept aside when building a machine learning model?
options: To check how well the model works on data it has not seen
To increase the amount of training data
To remove the labels from the data
questions.explanation: Testing on unseen data shows whether the model has genuinely learned rather than memorised.

questions.q: A face-recognition model trained mostly on photos of people of one skin tone makes more errors for other people. The main cause is
options: Unrepresentative training data leading to bias
The photos were stored as binary
questions.explanation: A model reflects the data it learns from; skewed data produces unequal accuracy across groups.

questions.q: A model scores almost perfectly on its training data but poorly on new data. This problem is called
questions.explanation: Overfitting means the model has memorised the training examples instead of learning general patterns.

questions.q: Give two reasons why an AI system may give a wrong answer even though it appears confident.
questions.answer: The training data may be incomplete, biased or out of date, so the system has not learned about the situation. Also, AI finds statistical patterns rather than truly understanding meaning, so it can make mistakes on unusual cases or produce plausible but incorrect output.
keyPoints: Unusual inputs outside what it was trained on
questions.explanation: AI output should be checked by people, especially for important decisions.
